title: Interactions between dynamic/static ferrite recrystallization and austenite reversion in medium Mn steel
abstract: The microstructural evolution of a medium Mn steel (MMnS) during intercritical warm deformation at varying strain rates and subsequent annealing has been systematically investigated. The resulting microstructure is strongly influenced by the competitive or cooperative interactions between dynamic/static ferrite recrystallization and austenite reversion, which are highly strain-rate dependent. Rapid deformation provides more nucleation sites and enhances the driving force for static austenite reversion during subsequent annealing, while significantly suppressing static recrystallization (SRX) in ferrite due to intense competition. This leads to the extensive formation of fine austenite grains with a banded distribution along elongated ferrite grain boundaries. In contrast, under slow deformation, dynamic ferrite recrystallization (DRX) and dynamic austenite reversion may act both competitively and cooperatively. This results in the dynamic nucleation of austenite at equiaxed ferrite grain boundaries and ultimately produces a necklace-type distribution. These findings offer new insights into accelerating austenite reversion kinetics and tailoring austenite grain characteristics in MMnS through precise control of deformation parameters.
